narr: Abundant moisture, in combination with strong daytime heating, provided the fuel for robust thunderstorm development along a quasi-stationary front located across the southern Texas Panhandle late on the afternoon of the 31st. Strong instability and moderate wind shear allowed the storms which formed to quickly become severe and gain mid-level rotation. The rotating storms were efficient at generating hail, including very large hail at times. Several locations near Memphis (Hall County) and Tulia (Swisher County) reported hail as large 3 to 3.5 inches in diameter. The giant hail, bigger than baseballs, destroyed windshields on numerous vehicles on US Highway Highway 287 in Hall County. The intense and excessive rainfall flooded out a number of roadways across the southeast Texas Panhandle, including in and around Memphis. This event carried over into the early morning hours of June first.
ev: Numerous thunderstorms repeatedly trained over portions of the extreme southeastern Texas Panhandle causing widespread flash flooding across Hall County. Several roadways were either flooded or completely washed out. Farm to Market Road 2472 near Plaska was washed out. Additionally, Farm to Market Road 1041 near Texas State Highway 256 southwest of Memphis was reportedly washed out.
